The Harbor Park Model RV Enables Comfortable Tiny Living Without the Usual Space-Saving Compromises
24 photos
Photo: Cavco Industries
Tiny living has been around for decades, but it has never been more popular than it is these days. It seems that the movement has entered into a new era, having picked up more steam lately due to real estate constraints and people's desire to live more intentionally.
Now, tiny houses, be they on wheels or on foundation, are posed as highly practical alternatives for individuals looking to escape the financial weight of mortgages or high rent. But many of those intrigued by the idea of living in a tiny house to lead a simpler life and carry less financial burden are worried they’ll have to sacrifice too much space or comfort.
If you, too, have these kinds of concerns, you’ll love the Harbor tiny house. This slightly oversized tiny home has all the residential amenities you’re accustomed to and feels right the moment you walk through the front door. Designed as a cabin on wheels, it offers both the simplicity and cozy charm of a traditional tiny home and the functionality and comfort of a full-size dwelling, making downsizing feel like an upgrade.
Harbor is built by Fairmont Homes, a manufacturer with decades of experience in the housing industry. Founded in 1971 in Nappanee, Indiana, the company became part of Cavco Industries in 2015 but it continued to create beautiful and functional compact homes whose construction uses high-end residential materials like finished drywall, steel I-beams, OSB sheathing, and robust fiberglass insulation. This thing alone is enough to understand that their homes are made for more than just occasional weekend stays.
Photo: Cavco Industries Stretching 45 feet (13.7 meters) long and 11.5 feet (3.5 meters) wide, Harbor is a park model tiny home that boasts a roomier layout compared to traditional homes on wheels and is designed to fit your real, everyday life with an inviting lounge with a built-in entertainment center, a spacious U-shaped kitchen with dining space, two downstairs bedrooms, and a large bathroom.
In total, you get 505 square feet (just under 47 square meters) of living space, with no ladders to climb or low-ceiling lofts to navigate, making everyday living more comfortable. Of course, a “tiny” home of this size comes with a trade-off: it’s less convenient to move than a conventional tiny house on wheels.
Due to its generous dimensions, it would require professional hauling and special permits to be towed on public roads, but it still remains an appealing downsizing solution for people who want a more permanent living arrangement and intend to keep it parked in one location for longer periods of time.
With Harbor, the emphasis is clearly less on taking it everywhere and more on making the interior feel comfortable and complete. And if we take a look at the picture gallery and the floor plan, it indeed seems like a complete home. The two-bedroom layout makes it suitable for family life, and the full suite of residential amenities means it’s well-equipped for full-time occupancy.
Photo: Cavco Industries This park model has not one but two entrances, and the main one is a double glass sliding door that leads directly into the central living room. Open and fitted with an L-shaped sofa, a coffee table, and an entertainment center, it feels like a proper lounge in a conventional home. The entertainment wall, which integrates a TV and a fireplace with a wooden mantel, is strategically positioned between two expanses of glass that provide beautiful views and bring in ample natural light.
The living room is seamlessly connected to the right with a huge U-shaped kitchen that wraps around the front area of the house. It features ample base and upper hardwood cabinets and a standalone dining table in the center, which could also serve as a kitchen island for additional counter space. A large front window and several transom windows keep the space luminous, while the neutral styling and stainless steel appliances give it a contemporary appearance.
Photo: Cavco Industries Fit for a chef, this cooking space includes a large, residential refrigerator, a full range, a range hood, a microwave, and a farmhouse-style stainless steel sink.
The secondary entrance door offers direct access to the more private areas of the house. It opens into a hallway with doors to the bathroom and the two separate bedrooms. The master bedroom is located at the very rear of the house and has all the attributes of a conventional room, with a comfortable bed, space to walk around it, nightstands, and plenty of storage solutions, including overhead cubbies and a full wardrobe. There is also space for a wall-mounted TV, while two windows keep the room luminous and airy.
Photo: Cavco Industries The other bedroom is a bit smaller and is designed for kids with built-in bunk beds and a closet. Next to the bunk room is the bathroom, which is compact but well-equipped. It features a fully-tiled standing shower with glass door, a vanity with an elongated counter, a toilet, and a mirrored medicine cabinet. Harbor also includes a dedicated space for a washer/dryer with hookups already available, a floor-to-ceiling general closet, and a furnace closet, adding more convenience for full-time living.
Built on a heavy-duty quad-axle trailer, the Harbor park model tiny home features a modern exterior with Royal Dutch lap vinyl siding, a metal roof, ventilated soffits, and breathable mesh underbelly. This model is part of Cavco Homes’ Country Manor series and is only available in Canada, with pricing depending on the dealer you choose to work with.
